Ravi (AE): FYI customer (LargeBank) asked for an on‑prem airgapped POC. Key asks: secure bundle delivery, signed SBOM, cert rotation offline, and an agreed upgrade cadence. They want to run for 2 weeks. Can we scope what we can promise?
Nina (SE): Short answer: yes, but we need to be explicit about assumptions. Proposal: 1) Seed bundle (operator + runtime) on USB image; 2) Upstream minibundles (rsync-style deltas) for security patches; 3) One offline cert rotation run.
Ravi (AE): Good. What are the minimal preflight checks for their infra team? They only have one infra person allocated.
Nina (SE): Preflight checklist (concise): - Verify kernel & driver versions - Confirm GPU/CPU and disk space - Ensure a signed root CA or a provisioned signing key - Check offline host clocks or internal TSA availability - Provide checksum & signature verification steps
Lara (Ops): Ops caveats: chain-of-custody requirement -> we must provide timestamped signatures and an SBOM signed with an HSM-backed key if possible. If HSM not available, use KMS with export controls documented. Also recommend minibundles < 4GB for USB delivery.
Tom (PM): Commercial constraints: sealed/offline packaging and custom signing are billable. Recommend: one-time prep fee (eng + package work) + per-bundle signing/validation fee. 24/7 cutover coverage is an add-on. I'll leave ranges in the scoping doc.
Ravi (AE): They asked about upgrade cadence: they prefer security-only patches quarterly and major upgrades up to twice per year. Can we support that?
Nina (SE): We can commit to quarterly security deltas during the POC and document major upgrade windows twice a year. Note: smaller deltas via binary diffs helps USB logistics. Hotpatch/no-reboot mode is higher risk and will require additional validation, so call that out as optional.
Lara (Ops): Practical runbook items to include: verification commands, offline CSR flow, signer key rotation steps, and a rollback path. Example verification snippet to give them:```# verify manifest and signature
sha256sum -c manifest.sha256
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify vendor_pub.pem -signature bundle.sig minibundle.tar.gz
```
signing-bot: airgap-bundle-2024-11-12 signed with key id SK-45; manifest and sbom attached to artifacts storage.
Nina (SE): Security questionnaire items we should prefill: signing key custody, SBOM generation cadence, offline cert rotation steps, patch cadence commitments, and acceptance test matrix. Attachables: airgap-runbook.pdf, signed-sbom.json, minibundle-manifest-example.json, offline-rotation-example.sh.
Tom (PM): Risks to call out in SOW: - Third-party vulnerability scanning (SCAP) in sealed networks may add 2-5 days if we need to run it ourselves. - If the customer demands zero external time sources, timestamping approach must be agreed (internal TSA or embedded timestamps). - Any request for hotpatching without restart is an additional effort.
Ravi (AE): Pricing asked: for signed bundles and a weekend on‑call window during cutover. Tom, can you include sample ranges and an explicit note that final pricing requires SOW signoff?
Tom (PM): Yes — I'll add ranges and mark all sealed packaging items as estimates until we confirm engineering scope.
Ravi (AE): Action items: Nina -> draft 1‑page scoping note + acceptance criteria; Tom -> commercial ranges and risk appendix; Lara -> runbook checklist and verification snippets. Please drop by EOD PT; I'll send to customer next morning.
Nina (SE): Will do. Acceptance criteria draft will include: 1) Seed install completes on at least one host; 2) Signed minibundle applied and validated; 3) Offline cert rotation executed and verified; 4) SBOM + signed provenance delivered; 5) Runbook handed off with 1 live walkthrough.
Lara (Ops): I'll add the chain-of-custody appendix and timestamp guidance.
Ravi (AE): Thanks team. I'll coordinate legal for SOW language around sealed delivery and chain of custody. :thumbsup:
